recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce the old BackboneElement/item[x] structure for FHIR-24995; future concerns about these AdverseEvent fields should be evaluated against the current repeating CodeableReference design from FHIR-46599.
issue_request: FHIR-24995 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request for R5 asking that the AdverseEvent item[x] elements introduced by GF#17237 be 1..1 because each was the only element in its BackboneElement, and asking that the pre-applied value set bindings be reviewed.
initial_application: The Jira-cited commit 4c4287bd97 added the GF#17237 AdverseEvent contributingFactor, preventiveAction, mitigatingAction, and supportingInfo backbone changes and explicitly noted pre-applied GF#24995 value set bindings. In that commit, the four item[x] rows were already 1..1 and carried the AdverseEventContributingFactor, AdverseEventPreventiveAction, AdverseEventMitigatingAction, and AdverseEventSupportingInfo example bindings.
additional_context: AdverseEvent is in the current build source through source/fhir.ini, and the authoritative source is now source/adverseevent/structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml. Later Jira FHIR-46599 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 and decided to remove these same single-child backbones by changing contributingFactor, preventiveAction, mitigatingAction, and supportingInfo to repeating CodeableReference elements. Commit 017e9edbd0 applied that decision, retaining the same value set bindings on the new CodeableReference elements. Patient Care minutes on 2024-08-08 also discuss FHIR-46599 and the single-child backbone pattern.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the old child cardinality was already 1..1 while the item[x] children existed, and the current specification is now correct under the later approved CodeableReference model where the child elements no longer exist.
